SRbb461ae6cd770197.source_meaning: Counsel Mr. Kunzru, appearing for the appellants (the sons) in Civil Appeal No. 57 of 1951 before the Supreme Court, argued that the phrase 'estate of Baldev Das deceased' in the compromise decree refers strictly to the property Baldev Das owned at the time of his death in 1935. He contended this interpretation excludes the separate shares of property obtained by the sons through the 1928 partition decree, as the father possessed no interest in those specific properties at the time of his death. This argument was made to oppose the attachment of the shops at Abdullaput, which the appellants claimed were their exclusive post-partition property and not liable for the father's pre-partition debt.
SRbb461ae6cd770197.reason: The source text explicitly records the argument made by Mr. Kunzru regarding the interpretation of 'estate of Baldev Das deceased' in the context of the partitioned property. The reading aligns perfectly with the observed content role of attribution by counsel during the appeal proceedings.
